reviews.comment: Just don't. Save yourself pain and tears. Worst prof OAT.
Liked him overall, accent made him hard to understand at times. He heavily encourages class participation so do yourself a favor and participate. It helps you stay focused on the content

Rangan seems kind but can be harsh. Decent prof but shows extremely little empathy for his students. I finished the 2nd exam (held the day before the drop deadline) 1 minute late and received a 0% because of it. I was forced to drop the class after maintaining a 96% all semester.

Uses a socratic dialogue teaching style (which is good conceptually), but interrupts students when they try to answer. Gets verbally and visibly frustrated with students for lack of participation, but ignores the fact that he interrupts them when they do chose to try and answer.

There is a midterm and a final (all MC) that are doable as long as you go to class and don't put them off till last minute, and you get a cheat sheet for each! He gives 2 HWs that are similar to the exams in material. There are group case studies that can be difficult - but if you go to class he gives a lot of great tips! Overall a good prof!
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are engaging because he ties the material to real-world examples. Toward the end of the semester, he offers a generous amount of extra credit, which can significantly boost your final grade - so don't stress too much if you didn't do well on the first exam. However, the exams carry a lot of weight, so study to prepare.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rangan is a sweet professor who cares about his students. The class is not a lot of work, so it is a good CBK to knock out if you have a heavier class load. He lectures the whole time, which is boring, and he rambles a lot. He gives a lot of extra credit. The third exam is the "final," but it is not cumulative. 1st and 3rd exams are easy.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Rangan is an amazing professor and is great at teaching Excel. He goes very in depth about everything, gives great feedback back, and will help you with anything as long as you ask. Attendance isn't required, but I would recommend going, otherwise you will get lost. As long as you put in the work and do the spreadsheets, its an easy A.
I would highly recommend you to not take his class. He does not help at all and the test is so hard.
Great prof as he teaches well and always connects materials to the real world, which really helped as the material was boring. Class was easy and exams are open notes. Curves are a plenty

You have to be racist or have a weak comprehension of English to say you can't understand him. He conveys material much better than most professors I've had, and he does it in an engaging way. You get to use notes when you take the tests so as long as you put in a reasonable amount of effort, it's not hard at all.

Professor Rangan is knowledgeable but his lectures are quite repetitive. BUSN 203 is an easy course in general, but the exams make up 75% of your grade so you must prepare for them (they are open note). Other than that, the Excel HW and quizzes should be easy A's.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has a ton of extra credit near the end of the semester, so if you're in a hole early don't worry. This class is basically a test on how much you can print out during the exam, as it is open note (unlimited notes). If you understand everything he gives you online, you'll easily succeed. If not, you'll do poorly. Don't go to lectures: no need.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Rangan made stats both fun and applicable! His lectures are socratic-style and really make you think. He provides sample exams and ch. practice which helps for exam prep. No regular h/w, but occasional Canvas quizzes, after-class exercises, and case assignments. Gives bonus points at end of semester dep. on grade distribution. Def recommend!!

I only got through Business 203 because of AI and Tutor John. This guy's lectures are horrible; you cannot understand him, and he talks SO MUCH. Beware of online pop quizzes. Check your canvas each day that class is in session because that's when quizzes are posted. Just go to tutor John, and you'll be good. Don't waste time reading the textbook.

The best way to describe rangan is mid. Class content isn't super difficult especially the last exam, but he's not a good teacher. I'm indian and even I couldn't understand him sometimes. The practice questions and hwks are solid practice for the exam (which is most of ur grade). i didnt attend class bcs the lectures were rambly and off topic.

I'm sure rangan is a nice guy outside of class, however, in class you cannot understand much of what he says. Along with that, his hand writing is chicken scratch. Exams weigh for 75% of your grade, so good luck if you do bad on one test, it tanks your entire grade. Would not recommend as a professor in the slightest.

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR!! I took statistics as a senior in high school (and did great), and then took this class as a second-semester freshman, so I still remembered lots about statistics. However, that did not show when it came to this class. His lectures are unclear, and what he says becomes irrelevant, making his tests very confusing.

DO NOT TAKE. Probably one of the worst professors at TAMU, if you have to take him use a tutoring service because that is the only way to actually learn anything. He calls his exams open note but then proceeds to change the rules regarding them with little to no warning and throws hissy fits like an entitled toddler. TAMU needs to fire this guy.

He is probably the worst prof at A&M. He lacks compassion & does not care about you at all.  He's hard to understand, is not understanding whatsoever if anything else goes on in your life, and tells you you can use your notes but then takes them away randomly during the exam and leaves you with nothing. Doesn't respond to emails either. DO NOT TAKE

Rangan seemed like a nice guy at the beginning of the year. Towards the end of the year, he started lashing out at students for not paying attention in class and finding help anywhere other than solely his material. No one ended up paying attention in class because it was hard to understand him and how off-track we would get from the material.

Really not sure why there are so many negative reviews. I thought Rangan was a great professor! He was very caring, he made lectures entertaining even though attendance was not required, he did not make us pay for a textbook, and test were very doable (they are open note, so if you have good notes the exams are easy As).

Rangan is a nice guy who cares about learning, but often veers off topic in class about random things and doesn't teach the material well. He makes the content way harder than it should be, and his tests are pretty hard. Should've been an easy A but he doesnt make it that way.

I could tell that this professor cared and wanted us to learn, but her often would ramble about unnecessary information. He made the class harder than it needed to be. Also, he was difficult to understand.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst professors I have had at A&M. His lectures are long and boring and he makes things overly complex. If you can take a different professor, do it.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor I have had at A&M, super heavy accent so you can't understand a single thing he is saying during his lectures. Packed two tests into one massive test which resulted in a large majority of the class doing poorly. Does not care about his students and has no compassion. DO NOT TAKE

Lectures are overly complex and very simple in format. He uses a lot of calculus terminology to describe things and write equations, which makes them much more difficult to understand than they should be.
Online resources and videos are your best friend here. Most of the topics are easy enough you can just Khan academy your way through the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I understand why this prof would have low ratings for 203, but for an upper level smaller class I think he does a good job. He does a good job of making sure you are prepared for the exams and not grading homework too hard. He is easier to understand when he doesn't have to talk to large group. Class is pretty easy while still useful.

I will give him credit, he tries to make the lectures interesting, but the topic is so boring that its impossible to want to pay attention. The class is very simple especially if you took AP stats, and there are open note exams.

Exams are worth 75% of the grade in this class and they are definitely not easy, but with about medium effort I was able to pull a very high B. He gives a ton of extra credit that can boost your grade almost an entire letter grade. Lectures super long, boring, and confusing.

Sudarsan Rangan is one of the best professors I have had so far. He is a very personable guy and cares about his students.His class isn't easy but really isn't hard. You just have to put good time and effort into the class and  you will succeed. He connects lectures to real world scenarios which is good because the lectures can get a little boring.

Professor Rangan is amazing at teaching. He explains the concepts very well and provides practice questions for every chapter which are very similar to the questions on the exams. 3 exams, no final, online quizzes, in class assignments, and case assignments. The class overall was not hard. He wants the best for all his students. HIGHLY Recommend!

If you are genuinely interested in learning about statistics, take Sudarsan. Unlike Hale, he emphasizes understanding the concepts. The exams are weighted heavily (75%), but he provides resources, and you can use a cheat sheet. Up to 4% extra credit, easy bonus assignments (very few!), and good pacing. Attend lectures and ask questions for an A.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Rangan is one of my favorite professors. He explains the content really well and his lectures are interesting. He tries to relate the content with real world business applications which makes a boring subject like statistics interesting. There are 3 exams worth 75% in total but he gives ton of resources to help you prepare for them.

Professor Rangan really cares about his students and tries his hardest to apply concepts learned in class to the real world. His lectures are engaging and you can find yourself truly understanding the concepts and their application. The class is exam heavy (3 exams, 25% each), but he gives you lots of resources to succeed and do well on the exams.

Class has a fair, reasonable structure. Gives lots of little bonus assignments for extra credit and lets you bring a cheat sheet for tests. Assignments are paced out well and he gives you lots of time to complete them. Tests aren't bad if you do the practice exam and look over the review. He's nice, and lectures use interesting real world examples.

He is a really good choice for this class. He doesn't require any outside textbook reading, exams are open note taken from home, and there are only a few assignments outside of class that are not difficult and only take about 10-15 mins to complete. His lectures made the content in the class very easy to understand and used interesting examples.

Don't skip class, you will have a really hard time if you do. If you show up and pay attention, all his test questions are from the lectures. He has open note exams and gives extra credit. If you don't like participating and want to read more, choose a different prof.

Dr. Rangan is one of my favorite profs at Mays. His class is tough but teaches real-world concepts that you can use in your internship or job. Some students choose to slack off, my advice is to take advantage of what he says so you can become competitive after college. His lectures are interesting but can also be tough. Extra Credit and open note.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures have difficult concepts that are hard to keep up with. He sets up homework to be "practice" for the exams which are not that difficult but then end up being nothing like the exam. Exams are almost like trick questions. He's disrespectful and is rude via email often. Do not recommend, the other profs may be hard but are probably better.

I had a pretty good time with this class. Statistics is pretty boring to me but if you go to class and take good notes you will be fine. He gives a few bonus assignments which was the reason I got an A. All assignments are online as well.

Professor Rangan was great -- his exam content comes almost entirely from lecture, so make sure to attend class. He really tried to make class as engaging and interesting as possible, and he gave us a couple of extra credit opportunities. I was not good at stats in high school but his lectures made sense, just take thorough notes of everything.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy, boring subject. Quizzes are not hard, but brush up on notes before attempting them. He lets you use your resources for exams, to include an excel sheet. USE EXCEL. Professor super friendly, and is more than willing to work with you on anything if you just ask. Responds to email immediately. Don't blow off the class and it isnt bad at all

A relatively straightforward class made confusing. Dr. Rangan does a great job of applying the concepts to a bigger scope, but it not very helpful for tests. There's a learning curve between the exam and course content, so you actually have to understand the content to succeed on tests. Lot's of other class activities, but mainly test heavy.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class has vanquished my prior knowledge of stats due to the confusing nature of lectures. Answer keys for practice problems and practice tests do not have worked out steps, so there is no way of knowing what you are doing wrong. He is passionate about SCMT but not the best at teaching statistics. This class is much harder than it should be.

Dr. Rangan is a difficult professor, but he's really passionate about Supply Chain Operations. He tries to make his lectures interesting, and I was really able to remember the points he made. His goal isn't for you to leave an expert in the subject, but for you to be able to understand the underlying concepts and apply them in your everyday life.

If you have a choice go ahead and take professor Hale 10/10. Horrible lectures/rants. Boring. Hard to want to go to this class. Not sure how this guy is a supply chain management advisor. Very impertinent and demanding.

Genuinely one of my least favorite professors ever. Not only is he a bad professor, he is incredibly rude and condescending as well. This man has made me cry. The material really is not that bad but he makes it 100x harder than it needs to be, and his thick accent doesn't help. Do yourself a favor and find another professor.

Rangan is very boring. He seems like a nice guy, but between his monotone voice and heavy accent, he makes it very hard to pay attention. When class starts, he just pulls up the slides and starts lecturing. And if you are a SCMT major, you have to take him at least one more time, plus he is the main adviser. SCMT 5/5 Rangan 2.5/5

Only reason I gave him a 2 is because he started to give extra credit towards the end of the semester. Buuuut the only reason he did that is because he saw the class average decrease throughout the semester. If you haven't cried in college and you take him... just wait on it.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: After first exam, you think you got a 100 but no. The questions are so tricky. At least 50% of test, (10 questions) are theory definition type tricky questions and there is few math. Whole class is based on theory. gives like 40 points extra credit towards the end. in class asignements easy. quizzes kinda hard, cases are easy, get a cheat sheet

Seems like a great guy, but did not like the tests given in this class. They are timed and most people are unable to finish. I felt very confident and ready going into the tests but ending up failing them. You don't really learn anything from the lectures. Very boring and difficult to pay attention to. Made things way harder than they actually were

This class is very annoying, the material is not hard at all. But you can feel pretty good going into an exam and still not do as well as you expected. 20 multiple choice questions at 5 points a piece leaves you very little cushion for mistakes. With the being said, he offers multiple chances at extra credit, so go to class. An A is doable.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He says not to buy the textbook but it makes the material 100% clearer. I went to a total of 5 classes and ended up with a 89.7 in the class, which does not translate to an A bc of his STRICT cutoff points. When I stopped going to class and started teaching myself my actually grades went up from 70 to 85 to 90 and then finally 94.

His last year of teaching 303 was the semester I had him. Im not sure if he made the tests harder for that very reason but it was extremely difficult. Tutor John tries to prepare you the best he could for the theory but good luck. Students receive 0s on exams for not using the right calculator. Didn't hold office hours until the second test.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: To get a good grade requires going to class! Going to class helps with the why aspect of his exams because his exams focus more on the "why" than on the "how" of a particular topic. He explains why we use a specific formula and how we identify the data to input in such formula.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This man spends 90% of each class talking about random scenarios/class notes from previous tests and 10% actually teaching the material that you need to know. He also uses the phrase which means so much that you will find yourself counting how many times he says it in one class instead of actually paying attention.

Supply chain 303 is supposed to be a simple statistics class. There is not a professor out there that could make such simple material unclear to their students like Professor Rangan does. He is a terrible teacher and lecturer, students are just able to get by due to the material itself being relatively easy.
Rangan is the literal worst ever. He spends most of the class period recapping previous material. He did not prepare us for the exam, and does not make himself accessible outside of class. beware.

Tests are very confusing and some are more difficult than others. However, he offers multiple extra credit opportunities. His lectures are really boring and the attendance is not mandatory, although he says it is. Study the practice exams and problems for the test and you should be fine.

The class isnt very hard, but just very annoying. His lectures are 75% recapping old material and 25% new material. You could honestly learn an entire 3 weeks worth of class in 2 hours of youtube videos. He has a thick accent. Tons of EC and you can bring your own cheat sheet for the tests

Rangan was my favorite prof at TAMU so far. He really cares for his students. If you're a SCMT major, I recommend taking him over Darcey because he will be your advisor, and he remembers his students. If you go to class and pay attention in lecture, you shouldn't have to study much outside of class (other than taking online quizzes and homework).

Dr. Rangan seems like a nice guy. He makes too much of an effort to cover WHY we do things rather than how to do them. His lectures seem to ramble on while he asks open ended questions to the audience. There is not really than much material, but the tests are worth 85% of the class. He does give 2.5% extra credit.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mr. Rangan is a class act. Extremely smart guy. Great teacher. Kids, just go to class, pay attention, and keep up with the material. You will be just fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Assignments are straightforward and given in class (must be in class to get assignment and due date, usually open for 24 hours). Offers lots of extra credit! Overall easy class if you go to lecture. Enjoyable professor!

Dr. Rangan was a fair professor. To be quite honest, the material is not difficult, and there's not a lot of it. Pay attention to in-class examples, quiz and homework questions: they show up again on tests. He is very caring and happy to take the time to explain concepts you don't understand.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Awful. He rambles on and on in class but doesn't do enough actual examples, and he ran out of time to even finish the notes before our last test. His accent also makes things kind of hard to understand. The material really isn't that hard; he just does a very poor job of explaining anything.

There were 4 exams in the class. The tests were hard. He goes over things slowly, and then rushes before the test to finish all the material. He thinks his test are fair, and he blames students and not himself for doing bad on them. He's not a fan of tutoring services, and he tries to make it so they don't help on the tests. He's a slow grader.

Only 2 tests: midterm and final, which together make up 80% of the course so if you do bad on one, you're screwed. I took this class in an honors section so it was smaller and he had a sign in sheet to track attendance. He's a nice guy, but not very fluent in English and it is so hard to understand him during his lectures most days.
No, Rangan is not easy.  That being said, he is easier than darcy.  I'd take him again.  Stat is a little difficult, and if I studied more I probably would have gotten an A.
Rangan is awesome! Super nice and makes the class really easy. Curves almost every test and there is no textbook or homework.
